correctness.rationale: For monic P of degree d and k>=1, P'P^(k-1)/d is monic of degree dk-1. For every f of degree <=dk-2, Green gives the inner product as level-boundary integrals proportional to ∮ f/P^k dz; the residue sum vanishes because f/P^k=O(z^-2) at infinity. Approximation by regular levels handles critical values. The area formula for a d-sheeted polynomial map gives ||P' P^(k-1)/d||²=pi(R^(2k)-r^(2k))/(dk). Differentiation of monic polynomials and cap(P^-1(disk_R))=R^(1/d) yield b_{dk}=sqrt(R^(2k)-r^(2k)) and normalized defect sqrt(1-(r/R)^(2k)); uniqueness follows positive definiteness of area Gram matrix. No assumption of simply connected filled set or regular boundary is needed.
